entries.definition: someone to whom private matters are confided
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Defines the friend entirely by what may be told them, making closeness a matter of trusted secrets rather than time spent together as in *companion*.

entries.definition: a person regarded very fondly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Pure fondness raised as high as the family goes, prizing the person without saying anything about trust or shared company.

entries.definition: informal term for a friend of the same sex
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and easy, and it specifies a friend of the same sex where *friend* leaves that unsaid.

entries.definition: a member of a learned society
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Membership as conferred standing — a learned society's name for one of its own, where *member* would only note that someone belongs.
examples: he was elected a fellow of the American Physiological Association

entries.definition: one of the persons who compose a social group (especially individuals who have joined and participate in a group organization)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat term for one of the people a group is composed of, joining and taking part included but no warmth or rank added.

entries.definition: someone accepted for membership but not yet fully admitted to the group
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names a person by an admission still unfinished, accepted but held short of the settled standing *member* assumes.

entries.definition: a female person who is a fellow member of a sorority or labor union or other group
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Turns fellow membership of a sorority, a union or any other group into a family tie between women, warmer than the bare enrolment *member* records.
examples: At the meeting she thanked her union sisters for their support.

entries.definition: a woman who cohabits with an important man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A term of position rather than accusation: it fixes a woman by the household she shares and the standing of the man in it, saying nothing about marriage being broken.

entries.definition: an adulterous woman; a woman who has an ongoing extramarital sexual relationship with a man
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The censure is inside the definition rather than added by the speaker, since the word names the relationship as adulterous and ongoing; where *concubine* marks a living arrangement, this marks a breach.
examples: He kept a mistress in town for years while his wife stayed in the country.

entries.definition: an old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A diminutive fastened to any old woman at all, grandmother or not - familiar where *mother* is deferential, and it shrinks her to her age.

entries.definition: an ugly evil-looking old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Repulsion with nothing added: the same ugly, evil-looking figure as *witch* but stripped of any power, so it jeers where *witch* recoils.

entries.definition: a term of address for an elderly woman
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A way of speaking to an old woman rather than a way of describing her, and it lends her the standing of kin in the act of addressing her.
examples: The soldier took the old woman's basket at the gate and said, "Let me carry this for you, Mother."

entries.definition: an ugly evil-looking old woman
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts menace behind the ugliness - she does not just look evil, she looks capable of it, which is the charge *hag* leaves off.

entries.definition: a male slave
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and legal in cast, naming the same owned condition as *slave* but of a man specifically, and at a cooler distance.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Damns the person themselves as something another has made and can direct at whatever unpleasant or dishonest work is wanted, where *tool* damns only their usefulness.
examples: He was no free man in that office, only a creature of the duke.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous with a note of ridicule — the person moves and acts, but the strings and the dishonesty behind the act belong to whoever works them.

entries.definition: a person who is owned by someone
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Drops the metaphor that *puppet* and *tool* run on and states ownership flatly, which is what makes it the heaviest word here.

entries.definition: a person who is controlled by others and is used to perform unpleasant or dishonest tasks for someone else
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coldest of the three: the person is an implement taken up for the dirty or merely unpleasant jobs, valued for nothing but being handled.

entries.definition: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hardens the same non-belonging into strangeness of kind - where *stranger* says merely unknown here, this makes the person incompatible with the surroundings.

entries.definition: anyone who does not belong in the environment in which they are found
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unjudging - it records only that the person is not of this place, and leaves open that they might belong somewhere else just as ordinarily.
examples: After ten years in the village he was still treated as a stranger.

entries.definition: a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blunt name for the thing, stating the secrecy or the illicitness plainly where *intimacy* muffles it.
examples: He kept the affair hidden from his wife for years.

entries.definition: a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lends the secretive or illicit tie a romantic, faintly literary glamour that *affair* denies it.

entries.definition: a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the same secretive or illicit tie by its closeness alone, a soft covering over what *affair* says outright.
examples: Their intimacy was discovered, and both families were disgraced.

entries.definition: the psychological state of being irritated or annoyed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest way to say it, the state at everyday strength without the weight *vexation* adds.

entries.definition: a state of irritation or annoyance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and faintly belittling — a state one is *in*, flared and conspicuous, next to the settled condition *vexation* describes.

entries.definition: a lack of patience; irritation with anything that causes delay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the state by what it lacks, and pins the irritation to one cause — anything that makes you wait.
examples: I shall not sport with your impatience by reading what he says on that point.
Her impatience for this second letter was as well rewarded as impatience generally is.

entries.definition: the psychological state of being irritated or annoyed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the state, carrying no verdict on whether it is deserved.

entries.definition: a lack of patience; irritation with anything that causes delay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same shortage of patience heard as agitation that will not settle under delay, where *impatience* hears a demand that things move.
